question: Does the unchanged two-witness surface rejector add decision-changing zero-assignment value over rank-only registered-surface matching on a new 3RScan family with same-class missing and extra candidates?

predecessor.observed_gap: The predecessor reached F1 1.0, but rank-only surface matching also reached F1 1.0 on that fresh physical-target cohort, so the witness rejector had no established incremental value.

method_sources.name: Zero-Assignment Constraint for Graph Matching with Outliers
method_sources.used_idea: Treat unmatched nodes as explicit all-zero rows or columns instead of forcing a complete permutation.

method_sources.name: Predictor-Rejector Multi-Class Abstention
method_sources.used_idea: Evaluate the independent rejector against the unchanged predictor and require fresh incremental gain.

frozen_cohort.selection_order: Exclude every reference scan family and physical reference target in the nine consumed cohorts. Group the frozen candidate rows by scan family in first-occurrence order, then by normalized semantic class in first-occurrence order. Choose the first family/class with six distinct surfaces on both scans and take its first six rows in the existing area-proxy order. Declare rows one and two registration witnesses and rows three through six evaluated targets before any surface distance is computed.
frozen_cohort.scenario_contract: Use one closed-six scenario, one query-extra scenario, one reference-extra scenario, and all twelve ordered balanced missing-plus-extra swaps across the four evaluated same-class targets. Every scenario contains both witnesses on both sides.
forbidden: using surface distances to choose the family, semantic class, targets, witnesses, or swaps
changing the witness count or identities after replay
multiplying, adding slack to, or tuning the predecessor witness ceiling rule
dropping any of the twelve balanced swaps after observing outcomes
claiming statistical coverage from two engineering witnesses
using target IDs inside evaluated correspondence ranking

frozen_model.surface_score: The unchanged predecessor negative symmetric median nearest-surface distance after the official rigid scan transform.
frozen_model.witness_ceiling: The unchanged larger of two predeclared witness correspondence residuals, with no multiplier, quantile, or learned parameter.
frozen_model.rank_only_baseline: Strict reciprocal row-and-column maxima on the same surface score, with no absolute rejector.
frozen_model.complete_baseline: Complete Hungarian assignment on the same surface score.
frozen_model.witness_zero_assignment: An edge must satisfy the rank-only baseline and its distance must not exceed the witness ceiling; otherwise the relevant node remains unmatched.

decision_gate.rank_only_incremental_opportunity: Rank-only must emit at least one false positive across the frozen scenarios.
decision_gate.witness_true_matches: All frozen truth correspondences across all scenarios.
decision_gate.zero_assignment: Exact unmatched reference and query sets in every frozen scenario.
decision_gate.no_true_match_regression: Witness-calibrated true positives must be at least rank-only true positives.
decision_gate.single_replay: One replay on the frozen scan-family-disjoint same-class cohort; do not tune or rerun after outcome.

claim_boundary: A pass is same-provider but scan-family-disjoint real-geometry Development evidence that the unchanged two-witness rejector adds decision-changing value over rank-only registered-surface matching for truth-proposed same-class indoor door targets under bounded missing/extra roster constructions. The witnesses, semantic labels, surfaces, and rigid transform remain privileged provider evidence; two witnesses have no statistical coverage guarantee. It is not raw-phone perception, open-world discovery, door detection, a portal aperture, named entrance, ownership, access, traversability, waypoint, arrival, HANDOFF_READY, provider-independent confirmation, user benefit, or mobility safety.
